qaPortal.title: From manual QA audits to a self-service data portal
qaPortal.intro: Anonymized case from my work as a Business Analyst at a contact-center (BPO/CX) operator with dozens of client accounts. Every name and number shown here and in the demo is fictional.
qaPortal.role: My role: Business Analyst and developer — discovery, requirements, solution design and a working pilot, aligned with the reporting and data teams.
qaPortal.demoNote: Fictional data · runs in your browser · try “View as → User”
problem: Each client account kept its QA evaluations in its own spreadsheet, with different columns, tabs and score scales.
A template tab had to be added to every file and the results were compiled by hand, one account at a time.
File links arrived by chat to a single person: when that person was out, the process stopped.
Some formulas averaged averages, so a quiet week weighed the same as a busy month.
discovery: Interviews with the reporting team, account owners and the data team.
Audit of each account’s calculation against its raw data, documenting every difference.
For each report: who uses it, which decision it supports, where the data comes from, how often it refreshes and what happens when it fails.

requirements.title: Never count an evaluation twice
requirements.description: The same evaluation can appear in a copy of the file or be corrected by adding a new row.
requirements.given: Given two copies of the same evaluation (same key columns)
requirements.when: When the account file is loaded
requirements.then: Then only the most recent copy counts, and the person loading the file sees which row was kept

requirements.title: A renamed column must not break an account
requirements.description: Accounts change their files without notice; a partial load would silently distort the results.
requirements.given: Given an account renames a mapped column in its file
requirements.then: Then nothing new is loaded, the previous data is kept, and the account user can map the new column and reload

requirements.title: Weighted QA score for any period
requirements.description: Managers compare months, weeks and custom ranges across countries, accounts and lines of business.
requirements.given: Given evaluations stored with a numerator and a denominator
requirements.when: When a user selects a month, week or custom range
requirements.then: Then the score is the sum of numerators ÷ the sum of denominators, never an average of averages

decision.title: Stakeholder decision: who approves data deletions?
decision.description: Deleting or reloading data changes the reports of a whole account, so the approval flow had to balance control and speed.

stakeholders.position: A dedicated approver should sign off every deletion and reload.
Requests should not wait for one person; any admin should be able to approve.

decision.resolution: Resolution: two roles (Admin and User). Any admin approves and the action runs immediately, protected by a 7-day backup and a full activity log.

flow: Wizard maps and tests the file
features: Mapping wizard that tests the real file before saving
One generic engine; each account’s rules are data, not code
Requests and approvals with email alerts
Two roles with per-account data isolation
Swappable destination: spreadsheet in the pilot, data warehouse next
outcomes: A working pilot with several accounts and a self-service portal.
Calculation issues found and documented before they reached the dashboards.
A target architecture and migration plan proposed to the data team.
qaPortal.confidentiality: Client, company and people names are omitted. The demo is rebuilt with fictional data and does not include the production code or data.

caseStudy.title: Evaluation metrics dashboard
caseStudy.intro: Anonymized requirements documentation from a real case: a dashboard showing quality evaluation metrics for a customer support team.

requirements.title: Fix the denominator on the evaluation percentage widget
requirements.description: The widget calculated the evaluation percentage using the wrong denominator, inflating the number shown to supervisors.
requirements.given: Given an agent has gradable interactions in the selected period
requirements.when: When the dashboard calculates the evaluation percentage
requirements.then: Then the denominator must be the total gradable interactions, not the total evaluated interactions

requirements.title: Add a gradable interactions count widget
requirements.description: Supervisors need to see, at a glance, how many interactions were eligible for evaluation in the period, without manually cross-referencing another report.
requirements.given: Given a supervisor opens the dashboard for a given period
requirements.when: When they review the general metrics section
requirements.then: Then they should see a widget with the total gradable interactions for that period

openQuestion.title: Pending validation
openQuestion.description: I found that two stakeholders interpreted the same KPI differently. Instead of deciding for them, I documented both interpretations as an open validation point, which avoided building on a wrong assumption.

stakeholders.interpretation: The quality percentage should be the average of the scores obtained across all evaluations.
The quality percentage should be the percentage of evaluations that passed (pass/fail), without averaging scores.
